actions: Continued the exact Figure-1 tau_p audit from the predecessor checkpoint using the public equations and the public run_parameter_sweep discretization for every public logspace point with tau_p>=0.010722672220103232 (indices 17..99 of np.logspace(-3,3,100)), 50 independently generated pattern/query realizations per point, N=30, K=100, six flipped bits, Time=10, dt=0.001, tau_x=1, T=0.01.

Recorded both true last-observed soft-Hamming/perplexity and the public code's last-above-threshold values, plus public list-length convergence-time surrogates, finite first-passage indices, threshold recrossing flags, post-Euler negative gain events, and NaN-perplexity events.

Validated a newly observed low-tau numerical issue against the literal scalar public update: p is clamped only at the start of an Euler step, can become negative after dp integration, and entropy/perplexity are then evaluated before the next clamp. The dynamics can recover on later steps, so these NaNs may be silently omitted rather than crash the sweep.

tau_p_sweep_progress.remaining_reason: The public rule uses dt=tau_p*0.05 below 0.01; exact Time=10 integration becomes computationally stiff. These 17 points are explicitly unresolved rather than extrapolated.

protocol.seed_policy: For reproducibility, public point index i uses torch Generator seed 202608260804+i; each point uses fresh random KxN binary memories and six unique random query flips for each of 50 repetitions.
protocol.public_observable_semantics: distance is computed from pre-x-update z=tanh(10*x), while perplexity is computed from post-p-update normalized p, matching Dynamical_regimes.py.
protocol.true_endpoint: last distance/perplexity observable actually evaluated before official break or Time=10
protocol.public_reported_endpoint: distances[-1] and perplexities[-1], where lists append only while distance>0.01 and perplexity>1.1
protocol.recross_test: flag any finite trajectory that goes below a reporting threshold and later rises above it before official termination

endpoint_reporting_mismatch_confirmed_br.result: For points where at least half of repetitions officially converged by Time=10 (through tau_p=10 in this fixed-seed audit), the median public last-above-threshold error exceeded the median true endpoint error by 0.0117078 to 0.0332623 soft-Hamming units. The corresponding perplexity median gap ranged from 0.0001324 to 0.1382588.
endpoint_reporting_mismatch_confirmed_br.interpretation: The public arrays named distances_final/perp_final are not end-of-run observables for converged trajectories; they are near-threshold pre-end values. This directly conflicts with reading Figure 1 as literal final-time error/perplexity, while leaving the underlying continuous-time convergence theorem and fixed-point equations untouched.

threshold_recrossing.interpretation: No empirical recrossing was found in the completed tau range under this seed set. Thus len(filtered_list)*dt does not acquire a large recrossing-induced occupancy bias here. It still differs from a literal first-passage timestamp by the code's indexing convention, and low-tau NaN omissions create an additional issue. Do not generalize the no-recross result to the unresolved tau_p<0.01 region or other tau_x/T sweeps.

post_euler_simplex_violation.mechanism: run_parameter_sweep reduces dt only when the swept value is strictly <0.01. The first three public logspace points above 0.01 therefore use dt=0.001. In the literal public Euler update, p is clamped before dpdt but not projected/clamped after p<-p+dpdt*dt before entropy; negative coordinates can therefore make log(p+1e-10) invalid for a step. The next iteration clamps p and may recover.
post_euler_simplex_violation.scope: This is a numerical-integration/observable validity defect in the published script for the tested low-above-0.01 points. It is not evidence against the model's continuous-time simplex dynamics.

finite_horizon_transition.interpretation: The public-paper qualitative statement that apparent performance worsens beyond tau_p around 10 because Time=10 ends before convergence is reproduced in this fixed-seed audit.

quality_notes: An earlier exploratory vectorized implementation in this physical run used the unclamped pre-step p as the Euler base and produced spurious recrossing/NaN behavior. Those exploratory outputs were discarded. All persisted statistics above come from the corrected literal public update p_base=clamp_min(p) before both the Euler base and dpdt.
No claims are made for the 17 unresolved tau_p<0.01 points.
exact_next_action: Finish public tau_p indices 0..16 (0.001 through 0.009326...) with the literal dt=tau_p*0.05 rule using rowwise/stiff-safe exact integration and the same corrected collector; specifically test whether post-Euler negativity/NaN disappears under the smaller official dt and whether any threshold recrossing appears there. Then rerun the full tau_p sweep with a positivity/simplex-preserving numerical update or sufficiently smaller dt as a sensitivity control, keeping the continuous model equations fixed, to quantify how much Figure-1 endpoint/convergence curves depend on the public Euler discretization. After that, resume the planned matched instantaneous-softmax versus finite-tau tests across T and tau_x to search for a regime where slow routing itself has a statistically robust benefit.
